title: Groq LPU-v3 captures majority of OpenRouter Qwen3.6-Max-Preview routed traffic by Q4 2026
body: By Q4 2026 Groq's LPU-v3 Inference Network captures more than 50 percent of OpenRouter's routed Qwen3.6-Max-Preview-235B request volume on the platform's evals-on-the-fly routing primitive, displacing the Together AI plus Fireworks AI plus DeepInfra plus Hyperbolic plus Lepton AI plus Alibaba Cloud Model Studio cohort that carried the model card through its Thursday May 28 integration cycle on five hosted providers wired in inside the first six trading hours of the U.S. session. The Thursday tape carried three operational features the cohort treats as the green-light pattern that lets a single hardware-stack vendor capture the cost-sensitive routing tier inside two earnings cycles. First, Groq's Thursday hosted-endpoint price sheet listed Qwen3.6-Max-Preview-235B at $0.31 per million input tokens — the lowest per-million floor in the OpenRouter cohort and an 11-cent undercut from the Alibaba Cloud Model Studio $0.42 Thursday-flip — which lands inside the platform's price-elasticity sensitivity band for the model-agnostic agentic workloads on Cursor, Cline, Aider, and Continue.dev that Alex Atallah's Thursday status note flagged as defaulting Qwen3.6-Max-Preview as substitute for Claude Opus 4.7. Second, Together AI cofounder Vipul Ved Prakash's Thursday-afternoon note recorded the LPU-v3 first-token-latency on the Qwen3.6-Max-Preview reference workload at 0.082 seconds — the first sub-0.1-second cold-start reading the OpenRouter dashboard has ever recorded, against the cohort's blended median first-token-latency of 0.156 seconds — which crosses the latency floor at which routing managers route the cost-sensitive default leg to the lowest-latency-and-lowest-price endpoint without per-workload manual tuning. Third, the LPU-v3 production capacity of 1.84 ExaFLOPS BF16 across 18 data-center sites confirmed by Groq CEO Jonathan Ross on Thursday — a 3.2x lift over LPU-v2 — combined with the additional $1.4B 2027 capex commitment to expand to 36 sites by Q1 2028 reported by Datacenter Dynamics, removes the capacity-ceiling objection that had kept Groq off the default-routing tier on the prior LPU-v2 generation. The structural force is that once a single inference-stack vendor pairs the lowest per-million floor with the lowest cold-start latency on the same model card on a single trading day, with capacity sized at 1.84 ExaFLOPS and a confirmed 3.2x throughput uplift per rack measured at 38,420 tokens-per-second on the Llama-3.1-70B FP8 reference workload, and the cohort's customer-side routing logic on Cursor plus Cline plus Aider plus Continue.dev is already wired to default to the lowest-latency-lowest-price endpoint at platform-level rather than per-tenant, the share-shift from the five-provider cohort to the single LPU-v3 leg compounds across each weekly routing-table refresh. The most likely landing is that by Q4 2026 OpenRouter's traffic dashboard shows Groq LPU-v3 carrying more than 50 percent of Qwen3.6-Max-Preview-235B routed request volume, with the platform exposing a customer-facing LPU-v3-preferred routing-tier toggle behind the same evals-on-the-fly primitive that handled the Thursday integration cycle, and with at least two of the four cohort agentic clients (Cursor, Cline, Aider, Continue.dev) marking the LPU-v3 endpoint as the platform-level Qwen3.6-Max-Preview default. Bear case is that Nvidia's H200 cohort lands a competing fused-router kernel inside vLLM v0.11.6 or v0.12.x that closes the latency gap below 0.1 seconds before Q4, holding LPU-v3's routed share at 35 to 45 percent of cohort volume; absent that latency-closing response, Q4 2026 lands the LPU-v3 as the first dedicated inference-silicon endpoint to capture majority share of a frontier-class open-weight model on a multi-provider routing platform.

reasoning.given: Cohort price-elasticity band routes cost-sensitive defaults on Cursor/Cline/Aider/Continue.dev to lowest-floor endpoint
reasoning.so_that: Per-routing-refresh share shift compounds from five-provider cohort into single LPU-v3 leg across weeks
reasoning.landing: Q4 2026 OpenRouter dashboard shows LPU-v3 >50% of Qwen3.6-Max-Preview routed volume
reasoning.plain_language: A new AI chip launched at the lowest price and fastest speed, so it will grab most of the popular model's traffic by year-end.

summary: Groq's Thursday LPU-v3 launch landed the lowest per-million floor ($0.31) and first sub-0.1-second cold-start (0.082s) on Qwen3.6-Max-Preview-235B in the OpenRouter cohort. The cohort's cost-and-latency routing defaults on Cursor, Cline, Aider, and Continue.dev compound a share-shift toward Groq, landing LPU-v3 as majority-share endpoint by Q4 2026.
